stem: Radha invests $\mathrm{Rs}\,6000$ at $8\%$ per year, compounded annually, for $2$ years.

parts.text: Which claim correctly gives the amount after $2$ years?

options.text: After year $1$ the amount is $\mathrm{Rs}\,6480$; year $2$ interest is taken on $\mathrm{Rs}\,6480$, so the amount is $\mathrm{Rs}\,6480\times 1.08=\mathrm{Rs}\,6998.40$.
Each year adds $\mathrm{Rs}\,480$ on the original $\mathrm{Rs}\,6000$ only, so the amount is $\mathrm{Rs}\,6960$.
Compounding also covers interest paid out each year with the principal kept fixed at $\mathrm{Rs}\,6000$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: With annual compounding, year-2 interest uses the updated amount after year 1, not the original principal alone.

teacher.key_rationale: 6000×1.08=6480 after year 1; 6480×1.08=6998.40 after year 2. Simple interest on the original principal or treating paid-out interest as compounding both miss the updated base.
